Current trial credits on two of the accounts are nearly depleted and the teams are mid-run. I can attach a spreadsheet with account emails and a couple of usage screenshots.

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the details and the spreadsheet — sending thanks to Ben (sales ops) to help triage. A few quick asks so we can move fast:

- Can you confirm all accounts are owned by Pearson AI Labs and linked to the same billing domain?
- Can you attach the PO or procurement contact (if available) so we can align with finance?
- Do any of the accounts show unusually high spike patterns (e.g., same IPs or identical prompt/sequence signatures)?

We do offer short trial extensions for legitimate pilots, but we also have to run a quick abuse check when multiple accounts request credits in a short window. Ben will coordinate with ops; we typically pause additional credits until the verification completes to avoid potential credit stacking.

Ill keep this on my radar — we want to make this work.

Best,
Grace

Grace/Neha — forwarding the Pearson request. Quick flag: I pulled the account list Aisha sent and cross-checked against our records. Two of the account emails have been used to create separate trial signups in the last 60 days and show overlapping billing hints (same payment method hashes). I'm attaching a small CSV with the account map and our notes (pearson_account_map.csv).

My recommendation: put a temporary hold on any additional credit allocations and run the abuse checklist below before we approve anything:

- Verify corporate domain ownership and billing relationship (procurement PO or vendor contact).
- Check for IP overlap or identical request patterns across accounts.
- Look for recent repeated extension requests from the same billing entity.

If this is a legitimate multi-team pilot, we'll set up a consolidated corporate seat and offer a scoped extension under a single billing entity. If it's coordinated multi-account usage to game credits, we should refuse and escalate.

Ben
Sales Ops
Attachments: pearson_account_map.csv

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Short-term credits for parallel pilots

Thanks Ben — I reviewed the CSV and pulled recent telemetry for the accounts. There are three indicators that trigger our abuse playbook:

1) Two trial accounts created within 48 hours of each other with matching sequence length distributions and identical token:response timing on a high proportion of requests.
2) The billing hints point to at least one cached payment hash that matches another account we flagged last quarter.
3) The procurement email on file differs from the domain Aisha provided in the spreadsheet (procurement@pearsonai.com vs procurement@pearson-group.com).

Per policy, we should not top-up credits until Pearson provides company-level verification: signed PO or vendor onboarding form, and confirmation that these user accounts fall under the same legal entity.

I'll open an internal fraud ticket and request a deeper audit. For now, recommend we offer a 7-day limited sandbox lift (non-billable cap: 50k tokens total) to keep the pilots moving while we validate.

Neha
Security & Compliance

Hi Aisha — thanks for the fast follow. We want to support Pearson but also need to follow our abuse prevention steps. Heres what we can do immediately:

- We can provision a 7-day sandbox lift with a 50k-token cap across the identified accounts to prevent interrupting active experiments.
- To approve any larger top-up or a full trial extension well need: a signed PO (company legal name and billing address), confirmation that the listed accounts are corporate (not contractor or personal), and the procurement contact on Pearson letterhead.

If you can send the PO or a vendor onboarding form and confirm the procurement domain, we will escalate for final approval. If procurement needs help with paperwork, I can loop in our finance ops contact.

If you prefer, we can also consolidate the pilots under a single corporate seat for simplicity.

Best,
Grace
